name: Flattery
definition: Praise aimed at a person's competence, expertise, or standing, offered to loosen their discretion before a follow-up question.
mechanism: Praise competence or standing so pride loosens discretion
recognition_cue: Praise out of proportion to the setting; being cast as the expert
countermeasure: Acknowledge professionally, do not expand; notice praise that precedes a question

name: Quid pro quo / volunteering / trading confidences
definition: An offer of a fact, favor, or personal disclosure made first so the target feels a social debt to reciprocate with information of their own.
mechanism: Give a fact or favor first so the target feels owed
recognition_cue: An unsolicited disclosure tied to a follow-up ask
countermeasure: Recognize the felt debt is not real; decline to trade

name: The Scharff technique
definition: A structured approach that pairs a friendly, non-confrontational tone with the impression the interviewer already knows most of what is being discussed, drawing confirmation or denial without ever asking directly.
mechanism: A friendly approach, an illusion of already knowing it all, never pressing, floating claims to confirm or deny, and downplaying what you reveal
recognition_cue: A pleasant conversation where the other person seems to know most of it and never actually asks; you leave feeling you gave away nothing
countermeasure: Recognize the profile; note that "they already know it" is a trap belief. Awareness alone is weak here, so this needs practiced response, not just a warning
